title: A systematic literature review of empirical research on ChatGPT in education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the early empirical literature on ChatGPT in education and asks how students and teachers have initially used ChatGPT, and what the main findings of those studies are. The review was motivated by rapid uptake of generative AI in educational settings and the need to understand both benefits and risks before broader adoption.

The study systematically searched five databases and screened peer-reviewed English-language empirical studies published up to April 10, 2023. Fourteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The included studies covered higher education most often, with one elementary education study and several studies that did not specify the level. Participants included university students, university teachers, both teachers and students, and elementary school teachers. Across the studies, ChatGPT was used for learning support, writing and language assistance, self-directed and personalized learning, teaching material creation, and productivity support.

The review concludes that ChatGPT can function as a virtual intelligent assistant for learners and as a productivity tool for educators, including for lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, and additional teaching resources. At the same time, the literature raises concerns about inaccuracy, hallucination, academic integrity, reduced critical thinking, and possible declines in collaborative or innovative skills with overuse. The authors emphasize the need for teacher training, clear guidelines, and further research on responsible integration of generative AI in education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review, but the underlying evidence base is composed of mostly small qualitative, mixed-methods, and quasi-experimental studies, with no meta-analysis or single well-controlled causal design reported in the review itself. The paper is peer-reviewed and methodologically transparent, but the evidence quality for the topic is limited and heterogeneous.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful benefits for learning support, teacher productivity, and some durable skills, but it does not provide pooled effect sizes and much of the evidence is descriptive or mixed. Reported impacts are therefore promising but still unclear at the population level.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of empirical studies on ChatGPT used by K-12 and higher-education participants for learning support, writing help, question answering, lesson planning, and teacher productivity; includes educational uses of ChatGPT as a virtual assistant, chatbot, and content generator.

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT was used to support writing and language tasks such as generating ideas, composing essays, summarizing, translating, paraphrasing, and checking grammar. The review reports mostly positive perceived effects on writing/language performance, but also notes concerns that overuse may weaken higher-order competencies and collaborative learning; no pooled effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Perceived writing/language support, writing task performance, grammar checking, paraphrasing, summarization, translation
finding.study_size: n=14 studies reviewed; relevant studies reported small samples, often <50

finding.finding_summary: The review summarizes several empirical studies in which ChatGPT supported mathematics learning by helping students understand problem-solving processes and complete geometry/problem-solving tasks. Reported findings were positive at the study level, but the review does not provide a pooled estimate or a single effect size.
finding.measure: Math problem-solving performance, understanding of problem-solving process, geometry task support

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT was reported to support learning across non-language, non-math contexts such as computer engineering, journalism, construction education, early education, and general homework support. The review describes improved understanding of concepts, hazard recognition, and completion of subject-specific tasks, but does not synthesize a numeric overall effect.
finding.measure: Subject-specific learning support, concept understanding, hazard recognition, homework/task completion

finding.finding_summary: The review reports that ChatGPT sometimes improved students’ engagement, motivation, and perceived learning experience, but also notes concerns that overuse may reduce motivation to attend class and undermine intrinsic engagement. These findings are descriptive and based on the set of empirical studies reviewed, without pooled quantitative estimates.
finding.measure: Motivation, engagement, learning experience, willingness to attend class

finding.finding_summary: This review identifies both positive and negative evidence for durable skills. ChatGPT was linked to improvements in reasoning, critical thinking, and problem-solving in some studies, but overuse was also associated with reduced innovative capacity, collaborative learning competencies, and higher-order thinking skills in others; the review cites this negative pattern in 3 studies (21.4%).
finding.measure: Critical thinking, reasoning, problem-solving, innovation, collaboration, higher-order thinking
finding.study_size: n=14 studies reviewed; negative pattern noted in 3 studies (21.4%)

finding.finding_summary: Teachers used ChatGPT to create lesson plans, generate quizzes, provide resources, answer questions, and preplan activities, which the review says improved productivity and reduced workload. Students also reported efficiency gains in completing writing and other academic tasks; the review is qualitative/descriptive and does not report a pooled effect size.
finding.measure: Teacher productivity/workload, task efficiency, time savings

finding.finding_summary: The review emphasizes the need for training, guidelines, policy development, and stakeholder engagement to support responsible ChatGPT integration in education. These are framed as implications and recommendations rather than measured institutional outcomes, and no effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Policy/guideline needs, training/support recommendations, governance implications
